title.en: Use relational, logical and assignment operators

say.en: 17 sweets shared among 5 friends: how many does each get, and how many are left? Python has an operator for each answer. In this lesson: Use arithmetic operators including /, //, % and.
Use relational, logical and assignment operators.
Use identity and membership operators.

body.en: Arithmetic operators: + addition, − subtraction, * multiplication, / division (always gives a float), // floor division (quotient rounded down), % modulus (remainder) and ** exponent. Relational operators compare two values and give True or False: ==, !=, >, <, >= and <=. The + operator also joins strings, and * repeats a string.

title.en: On the board: Arithmetic and relational operators

say.en: Take a equals 17 and b equals 5.
The modulus gives the remainder, and two stars mean power.
Floor division rounds down, towards minus infinity. So minus 17 floor-divided by 5 is minus 4, and the remainder is 3.
Relational operators compare two values and give True or False. Logical operators combine them.
Membership operators test whether a value is in a sequence: 3 in the list 1, 2, 3 is True.

title.en: Assignment, logical, identity and membership operators

body.en: Assignment operators store values: =, and shortcuts such as +=, −=, *=, /=, //=, %= and **=; x += 3 means x = x + 3. Logical operators and, or and not combine conditions. Identity operators is and is not check whether two names refer to the same object. Membership operators in and not in check whether a value is present in a sequence.

points.en: in, not in: is the value in the sequence?
